title: the three names you say in one breath
hookLine: Father, Son and Holy Spirit: said at every baptism, rarely explained
tomorrow: the visitor who came at night

cards: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. It's said over a baby at a baptism, at the end of a service, with a hand moving forehead, chest, shoulder, shoulder.
Ask someone who has said it their whole life what it means, though, and you may get a long pause, and then a picture of a shamrock. First, a guess.

teach.b: Christians say there is one God, and that God is Father, Son and Holy Spirit. Three persons, one God. Not three gods.
Not one God wearing three masks.
The word Trinity isn't in the Bible.

teach.h: IN THE NAME — ONE NAME, THREE.
teach.b: In the early 200s, a North African writer named Tertullian used the Latin trinitas to name something Christians saw all through the Gospels: Jesus praying to the Father, and promising to send the Spirit.
At the end of one Gospel, he sends his friends out baptizing in the name, singular, of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. One name. Three.
Every easy picture breaks somewhere. Water, ice and steam make it one God changing forms, an idea early Christians turned down. A shamrock makes each person a third of God.
So some teachers, as far back as Augustine, start somewhere else. One letter in the Bible says simply: God is love. And love needs someone to love.
Many Christians hear the Trinity that way: at the very center of God, a relationship.

how: Many churches baptize in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, and many say the Nicene Creed, a statement of the Trinity, in their Sunday services; Catholic, Orthodox and some other Christians also make the sign of the cross with the same words.

games.q: what's inside the word — tap the pairs.

s: the word Trinity appears in the Bible
it's a later word, from the early 200s, for what Christians saw in the Gospels.
one Gospel ends with Jesus sending his friends to baptize in the name of Father, Son and Holy Spirit
the name, singular: one name, three.
Christians say there are three gods
they say one God: Father, Son and Holy Spirit.

games.q: someone explains the Trinity as water, ice and steam: one thing, three forms. what did early Christians say about that kind of picture?
o: it turns God into one person changing forms, so they turned it down.
it's the only way to explain it.
games.why: they said Father, Son and Spirit are all there at once, not one after another. every easy picture breaks somewhere.

practice: One breath with the bell. Breathe in, and think of someone who loves you. Breathe out, and think of someone you love.
Then notice the love between you: something real, though you can't hold it in your hand.

wordCard.voice: The Trinity. One God, three persons: Father, Son and Holy Spirit. Second word on your strand.

orig.note: Latin: threeness, a trinity. Tertullian used it in the early 200s.

carryVoice: Your line: three, and still one. It's why that blessing says in the name, not in the names. Day two, done.
